title: Short-Form Video
article_body:
Short-form vertical video has fundamentally changed how people consume content online. YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels, TikTok, and Facebook Reels collectively capture more daily viewing time than almost any other category of media. The average person watches more than an hour of short-form video per day — a number that continues to grow.

Many business owners and marketing leaders resist short-form video because they don't personally consume it, or because it feels like a consumer entertainment platform rather than a business tool. This is a mistake rooted in personal preference rather than buyer behavior. The buyers researching your products and services are in this audience. Meeting them on platforms they already use is simply smart business.

## What Short-Form Video Is For

Short-form video is primarily an awareness tool. It reaches buyers who don't yet know you exist. When someone scrolling through Reels encounters a video that addresses a question they have — whether it's a quick tip, an honest comparison, or a moment from a longer expert conversation — they experience your brand for the first time in a way that feels natural rather than intrusive.

Long-form video builds depth with people who already know you. Short-form builds width — it expands the number of people who know your brand exists and have a positive first impression of it. Both are necessary, and they serve different goals.

## Bringing The Big 5 to Short-Form

Short-form video is an effective distribution channel for Big 5 content topics. A quick take on what drives cost up in your industry, a direct answer to a common buyer concern, a rapid-fire comparison of two options — these topics work in sixty seconds just as they work in ten minutes. The format is different, but the principle is the same: answer the questions buyers are already asking, honestly and on camera.

Comparison content performs especially well in short-form because viewers enjoy the format and find it useful. A thirty-second video that shows a clear side-by-side comparison of two options can stop a scroll and earn a follow from someone who was moments ago completely unfamiliar with your brand.

## The Repurposing Workflow

The most efficient path to a strong short-form presence is to build repurposing into your long-form production process. Every YouTube video, every recorded webinar, every expert interview contains moments that can be extracted, reframed vertically, and published as short-form clips. A single hour of long-form production can yield a month of short-form content with the right workflow.

This approach has a secondary benefit: short-form clips can drive viewers back to the long-form source. Someone who watches a sixty-second clip and wants to go deeper has a clear path to the full video. Short and long form are not competing strategies. They work together.

## What Makes Short-Form Perform

The algorithm on every short-form platform rewards two things above all else: click-through rate and retention rate. Your hook determines whether someone watches. Your structure determines whether they finish. High retention signals quality to the platform, which responds by showing the video to more people.

The guiding principle for short-form structure is: make them click, make them stick. Get to the point immediately. Remove every moment that doesn't advance the story or the value. End the video the instant the payoff is delivered. These are not suggestions — they are the structural requirements for short-form video that actually distributes. The Sticky 5 framework covers the specific mechanics in detail.

what_youll_learn: The average person watches over an hour of short-form video per day. Your buyers are in that audience.
Short-form video is a top-of-funnel awareness tool. It is different from long-form in purpose, structure, and how it is measured.
Short-form content performs best when it is fast, focused, and ends decisively. The Quit While You're Ahead Principle is critical.
Content that works well on one short-form platform generally translates to others. Plan for cross-platform distribution from the start.
Every long-form video you produce should generate multiple short-form clips. This repurposing workflow multiplies your investment.
Businesses that dismiss short-form video because they don't personally consume it are making decisions based on personal preference rather than buyer behavior.

key_questions.question: Should B2B companies be doing short-form video?
key_questions.answer: Yes. The buyers at B2B companies are the same people watching Reels and Shorts in their personal time. Meeting them on platforms they already use builds recognition and trust that carries over into professional decisions. B2B companies that are early to short-form in their category often develop significant awareness advantages.

key_questions.question: How do we come up with enough content for short-form?
key_questions.answer: Start with your long-form library. Every Big 5 video, Selling 7 video, or educational video you produce contains multiple moments that work as short-form clips. A twelve-minute YouTube video might yield six to eight Shorts. Build short-form into your production workflow rather than treating it as a separate effort.

key_questions.question: What makes short-form video perform well algorithmically?
key_questions.answer: Click-through rate and retention rate are the primary signals. Your hook (the first second or two) determines whether someone watches. The structure of your video determines whether they finish. High retention tells the algorithm the content is good, which leads to wider distribution.

key_questions.question: How often should we publish short-form content?
key_questions.answer: More frequently than long-form. Most companies aiming for YouTube Shorts or Reels target three to five posts per week. Consistency matters more than volume. Start with what you can sustain and build from there.

key_questions.question: Do short-form videos need professional production quality?
key_questions.answer: No, and over-producing them can hurt performance. Short-form audiences respond well to authentic, natural-feeling content. Good audio and decent lighting are the only technical requirements. Everything else is secondary to the quality of the hook and the value of the content.
